How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment
for agenda items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per
person (six minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time
limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note
that interactions between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings
are subject to the City’s Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 2, 2026

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Wu
 •  ROLL CALL

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. LGBTQ+ PRIDE MONTH

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  Consent Calendar items and on items of interest that are not on the Agenda but
  are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council requests separate discussion.

  A. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  B. STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY 2026-2027 [RESOLUTION NO. 26-
  18]

  California Government Code Section 53646 requires the annual review of the
  City’s Investment Policy at a regular meeting of the City Council. The

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  2
   requirement for an annual review of the policy is also stated in the City’s Fiscal
  Sustainability Policy (adopted April 2019 in the interest of fiscal accountability).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-18 adopting
  the 2026-2027 Statement of Investment Policy.

  C. APPROVAL OF A CHANGE ORDER TO CONTRACT NO. 25-12 WITH YUNEX,
  LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY IN THE AMOUNT OF $66,095 FOR
  ADDITIONAL CONDUIT INSTALLATION FOR CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM PROJECT #2-21-02 – TRAFFIC SIGNAL IMPROVEMENTS

  On December 16, 2025, City Council awarded the construction contract to
  Yunex, Limited Liability Company as the lowest responsive bidder, in the
  amount of $284,995 plus a 10% contingency, for video detection and closed-
  circuit television camera installation as part of the Capital Improvement
  Program (CIP) Adaptive/Traffic Responsive Signal Control Project (CIP# 2-21-
  01) and Traffic Signal Improvements Project (CIP# 2-21-02). Construction began
  on February 17, 2026, and the projects are 95% complete, but additional new
  conduit is required beyond the original specifications in order to complete the
  cable runs for the installation of video detection cameras at the intersections of
  Del Mar Avenue with Wells Street and Angeleno Avenue, respectively.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378(b)(4) of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the change order to Contract No. 25-12 in the amount of $66,095
  from the Capital Improvement Fund Measure R account 122-800-58-97-711
  to cover the additional cost of the electrical conduit installation; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a change order to Purchase Order
  9608 in the amount of $66,095.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  3
   D. APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO MEASURE R FUNDING
  AGREEMENT #9200000000MR53221 WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY

  On July 21, 2020, the City Council approved Measure R Funding Agreement
  #9200000000MR53221 with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Transportation Authority to accept $700,000 in Measure R funds that were
  reallocated from the State Route 710 North Project for the San Gabriel Traffic
  Signal Improvements Project (Project). The Project is approximately 95%
  complete, and is anticipated to be finished by September, 2026; however, the
  funds are programmed to lapse by June 30, 2026 under Amendment No. 1.
  Hence the necessity for a Second Amendment which would extend the
  expiration of the funding until the project is completed.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378(b)(4) of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Mayor to execute, on
  behalf of the City, Amendment No. 2 (Funding Agreement
  #9200000000MR53221) to the funding agreement with the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA) to extend the San Gabriel
  Traffic Signal Improvement Project (Capital Improvement Program 2-21-02)
  grant funding through June 30, 2027, ensuring the City remains eligible for
  reimbursement of project costs.

  E. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 730 AMENDING
  THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATED TO DOG LICENSING WITH
  THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HUMANE SOCIETY

  Ordinance No. 730 would amend the City’s Municipal Code provisions related
  to dog licensing to improve efficiency, enhance compliance, and better align
  with current animal services practices. Specifically, the ordinance replaces the
  City’s existing July 1 fixed license renewal cycle with a rolling expiration system
  based on the date of license issuance. At the May 19, 2026, City Council
  meeting, the City Council introduced Ordinance No. 730 and conducted the
  first reading. The ordinance is now presented for second reading and adoption.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  4
   Staff recommends that the City Council conduct the second reading by title
  only and adopt Ordinance No. 730 amending the San Gabriel Municipal Code
  to modernize the City’s dog licensing program by transitioning from a fixed
  annual renewal cycle to a rolling, date-based licensing structure.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PROPOSED CITYWIDE FEE SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-27

  The citywide fee schedule establishes user fees and charges for various
  department services. On an annual basis, the citywide fee schedule is reviewed
  and updated based on a combination of department input and the consumer
  price index in the Los Angeles Metro area. The proposed updated citywide fee
  schedule for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 is presented to the City Council for review,
  direction, and consideration of adoption.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-15 updating
  the Master Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2026-2027.

  B. ADOPTION OF THE FISCAL YEAR 2026-27 OPERATING BUDGET, CAPITAL
  IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM, AND APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT

  The City Council will hold a public hearing to consider adoption of the proposed
  Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Operating Budget, Capital Improvement Plan, and
  Appropriations Limit. With the utilization of reserves, the proposed General
  Fund budget is balanced, with revenues and transfers-in estimated at
  $59,273,000, and proposed expenditures and transfers-out totaling
  $59,908,000. Expenditures exceed revenues by $635,000 and will be funded by
  General Fund reserves. Across all City funds, total projected revenue is
  $96,850,000 and total proposed expenditures are $96,222,000. The proposed
  CIP includes $9,132,000 in new funding to support ten capital projects.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  5
   Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the
  proposed 2026-27 operating and capital improvement program budgets, and
  appropriations limit, and after receiving comments and testimony adopt the
  following Resolutions:

  1. Resolution No. 26-16 adopting the 2026-27 Operating Budget.

  2. Resolution No. 26-17 adopting the 2026-27 Capital Improvement Program
  Budget.

  3. Resolution No. 26-14 establishing the 2026-27 Appropriations Limit.

  C. CONDUCT A PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 26-
  23 VACATING AN UNUSED SIDEWALK AREA ALONG THE FRONTAGE OF
  261 SOUTH MISSION DRIVE AND RESERVING A PARKWAY DRAIN
  EASEMENT

  Parcel A is a section of unused sidewalk-area within the right-of-way easement
  along the frontage of the property at 261 South Mission Drive, which currently
  operates as a karaoke lounge. On May 5, 2026, based on staff’s
  recommendation and as required by the California Streets and Highways Code,
  City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-11 declaring the City’s intention to
  vacate Parcel A while reserving a parkway drain easement, fixing the time and
  place for a public hearing at the City Council meeting on June 2, 2026 for all
  persons interested in or objecting the proposed vacation, and directing staff to
  publish and post notices. After hearing and considering all the evidence offered
  by any interested persons at the hearing, if City Council finds that Parcel A is
  unnecessary for present or prospective public use, the City Council may adopt
  a resolution vacating it.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct a Public Hearing and consider all public comments regarding this
  matter; and

  2. Adopt Resolution No. 26-23 vacating an unused sidewalk area along the
  frontage of 261 South Mission Drive, subject to the reservation of a parkway
  drain easement to preserve the City’s right to access, maintain, repair,

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  6
   replace, and operate the City-owned drainage facility located within the
  vacated area.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. POLICY FOR  TECHNOLOGY  DISRUPTION  DURING  CITY  COUNCIL
  MEETINGS

  Senate Bill 707 requires the adoption of a policy, on or before July 1, 2026,
  which addresses disruption of technology for two-way remote public access
  during City Council meetings. At its meeting of May 19, 2026, the City Council
  authorized the purchase and installation of an integrated and updated audio-
  visual platform for two-way remote public access during City Council meetings,
  pursuant to Senate Bill (SB) 707. An additional requirement of the Bill is the
  adoption of a policy, on or before July 1, 2026, which addresses disruption of
  this telephonic or internet service.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the policy.

  B. DUMPLING AND BEER FESTIVAL: 2025 RECAP AND HIRING AN EVENT
  OPERATOR

  The Dumpling and Beer Festival (Festival) was introduced in 2015 to showcase
  the culinary aspect of the City and attract tourism to the Mission District. Over
  the years, the festival has grown into a community event that celebrates
  diversity and culture through popular food and drink. Each year the event
  attracts around 5,000-7,000 visitors and this number continues to grow. This
  report provides a summary of the planning efforts that contribute to the
  festival’s yearly success, a recap of the 10th Anniversary, and an opportunity to
  discuss the possibility of hiring an event operator.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  7
   Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Receive the report on the 2025 recap; and

  2. Review and approve the Professional Services Agreement with MPD Events
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 26-19 AUTHORIZING THE EXCEPTION OF THE 180-DAY
  WAITING PERIOD TO APPOINT CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS) RETIREE RUBEN SORIANO TO INTERIM
  POLICE CAPTAIN IN ACCORDANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION
  7522.56 AND SECTION 21221(H)

  Since August 2025, the Police Department has experienced vacancies at the
  Police Lieutenant and Police Captain positions due to retirements and other
  unexpected personnel matters. The department has since filled the Police
  Lieutenant vacancy, but the Police Captain position remains vacant pending the
  completion of an open-competitive recruitment. Police Captain is a critical
  position within the Police Department. The department maintains two Police
  Captain positions due to its size and scope of operations. The Police Captain
  reports directly to the Police Chief and oversees major divisions of the
  department. The position also serves as the department head and
  representative in the Police Chief’s absence. Ruben Soriano is a CalPERs retiree
  from the Alhambra Police Department and retired as a Police Lieutenant in
  December 2025 after serving the department for more than 28 years. Due to
  his extensive experience with local law enforcement, Mr. Soriano was identified
  as someone who could help the department during this transitional period for
  its leadership team.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-19, which
  provides an exception of the 180-day waiting period for CalPERS retirees and
  authorizes the City Manager to appoint CalPERS retiree, Ruben Soriano, to
  Interim Police Captain while a recruitment to fill the position on a permanent
  basis is completed.

  D. DISCUSSION AND DIRECTION ON PLACING A LOCAL SALES AND USE TAX
  MEASURE ON THE NOVEMBER 2026 BALLOT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 2, 2026  8
   San Gabriel has identified needs of over $100,000,000 in the upcoming years to
  protect services provided to residents and renovate or replace aging
  infrastructure. After considering several revenue options for meeting the unmet
  funding needs, a local Sales and Use Tax has been determined to be the most
  likely way to accomplish the funding for those future needs. A Sales and Use
  Tax of up to one cent could be considered by the City’s voters.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss and provide direction on
  placing a local Sales and Use Tax on the November 2026 ballot. Specifically,
  staff is seeking direction on whether to bring a ballot initiative forward and if
  so, at what rate, ranging from one-quarter cent to a full cent.

  8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, at
